description: The Maratha Empire was founded by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in the 17th century. It later evolved into a powerful Maratha Confederacy under the leadership of the Peshwas, dominating a large part of the Indian Subcontinent throughout the 18th century.

sections.title: Chhatrapati Shivaji and Early Maratha State
sections.description: The life of Shivaji Maharaj, his military campaigns, and the foundation of the independent Maratha Kingdom.

key_concepts.explanation: Shivaji's primary political and ideological objective, meaning self-rule or independence from foreign domination.
The guerrilla warfare and hit-and-run tactics utilized by the Marathas, which were highly successful in the hilly terrains of the Western Ghats.

historical_events.significance: Born in the Shivneri Fort; his parents were Shahaji Bhonsle and Jijabai.
Shivaji killed the Bijapur general Afzal Khan, which brought immense recognition to the rising Maratha power.
Signed between Shivaji and Mughal Commander Jai Singh; Shivaji had to surrender 23 of his forts to the Mughals.
Crowned as an independent ruler at Raigad; assumed the titles of 'Chhatrapati' and 'Haindava Dharmoddharak' (Protector of the Hindu Faith).

sections.title: Maratha Administration and Revenue System
sections.description: The administrative structure, military organization, and tax collection system of the Maratha Empire.

key_concepts.explanation: The Council of Eight Ministers that advised and assisted the Chhatrapati in state administration.
A tax comprising one-fourth (25%) of the total revenue, collected from neighboring states in exchange for protection from Maratha raids.
An additional 10% tax levied over and above the Chauth, claimed by Shivaji as his hereditary right as the supreme Deshmukh of the region.

key_associations.extra_info: Responsible for general administration and the highest minister of the empire.
Maintained the public accounts of income and expenditure.
Managed foreign affairs and relations with other states.
In charge of the intelligence department and the king's personal security.

important_facts.fact: Shivaji's regular state cavalry was called 'Paga', which consisted of 'Bargirs' (soldiers equipped by the state) and 'Siledars' (soldiers who brought their own horses and arms).

sections.title: The Peshwa Era and Maratha Confederacy
sections.description: The rise of the Peshwas during the reign of Shahu Maharaj and the decentralization of power into a Maratha Confederacy.

historical_events.significance: The first powerful Peshwa; he made the position of Peshwa hereditary and became the de facto head of the empire.
Achieved the greatest expansion of the Maratha Empire; known as the 'Warrior Peshwa' who severely weakened the Mughal Empire.
Fought between the Marathas and Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Abdali; resulted in a heavy defeat for the Marathas, shattering their dream of a pan-India empire.

key_associations.extra_info: Heads of the Maratha Confederacy and the chief executives.
A major military and political power in North India.
Controlled the Malwa region; Ahilyabai Holkar was a renowned ruler of this dynasty.
Led military campaigns in Central India, Odisha, and Bengal.
Exercised complete control over the Gujarat region.

sections.title: Anglo-Maratha Wars and Decline of the Empire
sections.description: The struggle for supremacy between the British East India Company and the Maratha Confederacy, leading to the empire's ultimate downfall.

key_concepts.explanation: A humiliating Subsidiary Alliance signed by Peshwa Baji Rao II with the British, which ended Maratha independence and triggered the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

historical_events.significance: Triggered by a succession dispute over Madhavrao II; ended indecisively with the Treaty of Salbai (1782), establishing 20 years of peace.
The Scindias and Bhonsles opposed the Treaty of Bassein; Lord Wellesley defeated the Maratha chiefs separately.
Maratha power was decisively crushed; the Peshwaship was abolished, and Baji Rao II was exiled to Bithur (near Kanpur) on a pension.

important_facts.fact: The last recognized Chhatrapati of the Maratha Empire was Pratap Singh, while the last Peshwa was Baji Rao II.
Nana Phadnavis was often referred to by the British as the 'Machiavelli of the Marathas' due to his exceptional political acumen and diplomatic skills.
